h: פָּרָשַׁת זָכוֹר, מַאֲמָר י״ב Parshas Zachor — Maamar Yud Bais

p: כָּל זְמַן שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק קַיָּים
"As long as the offspring of Amalek exists,
it is as though a wing covers the Face;
once his offspring is lost from the world,
'your Teacher shall no longer be hidden,
and your eyes shall see your Teacher'"
The matter is that this power,
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה כָּנָף מְכַסֶּה אֶת הַפָּנִים
that no wing should cover the Face,
הוּא עַל יְדֵי טַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
comes through the dew of Torah she'b'al peh,
which derives from the Dew of Atika,
as we have said many times
עַל פָּסוּק תִּזַּל כַּטַּל אִמְרָתִי [דְּבָרִים לב, ב]
on the verse "My word shall flow like dew" (Devarim 32:2),
which alludes to Torah she'b'al peh.
(מִדְרָשׁ חֻקַּת רַבָּה יט, ו; תַּנְחוּמָא ח)
כָּל יְקָר רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ [אִיּוֹב כח, י]
this is Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues;
things that were not revealed to Moshe
were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues" —
the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (מְנָחוֹת כט, ב)
And this is the meaning of what they said (Menachos 29b):
that when Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, saw
that they were weighing his flesh in the meat market,
this is Torah and this its reward?!"
so it arose in thought before Me."
he would ascend to the root, Atika,
which is above the level of thought;
and this is why they said specifically "in thought before Me,"
וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז רֹאשׁ הַפָּסוּק [יְשַׁעְיָה שָׁם]
And to this alludes the beginning of the verse (Yeshayah, ibid.):
bread of distress and water of oppression" —
that is, in the attainment of Torah she'b'al peh,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה וְלֹא יִכָּנֵף עוֹד מוֹרֶיךָ וְגוֹמֵר
and through this, "your Teacher shall no longer be hidden...":
you will merit the level of the Dew of Atika,
which is the light of Torah she'b'al peh.
"It was the time for reciting Shema, etc.;
אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו רַבֵּינוּ עַד כָּאן
his students said to him, 'Our master, this far?'
He said to them, 'All my days,' etc.,
until his soul departed with 'Echad,' etc."
This was because he sensed in his soul
his soul would ascend to the ultimate unity,
with attachment to the holy Atika,
the level of "in thought before Me," as mentioned above.
And as is known, he was one of the Ten Martyrs,
שֶׁהָיוּ לְהַשְׁקִיט קִטְרוּג שֶׁל הַסָּמֶ״ךְ מֵ״ם
who served to silence the accusation of the Samech-Mem,
who accuses regarding the holiness of the covenant:
טוֹל מַה שֶּׁבָּחַרְתָּ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל [מַאֲמָר ח]
"Take what You have chosen," as mentioned above (Maamar 8).
only into the hand of the offspring of Yosef,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו טַעֲנָה בְּעִנְיָן זֶה
because there is no claim against him in this matter,
as they said in Tanchuma (Ki Seitzei 10).
And the slight taint there was upon him
from the ten drops that came forth, etc.
in the elevation of his soul's attachment to the holy Atika.
וּבָזֶה נִכְנַע כֹּחַ עֲמָלֵק מִכֹּל וָכֹל
Through this the power of Amalek was utterly subdued,
that this is the essence of subduing the power of Amalek.
"This is Torah and this its reward?!"
אָמַר לָהֶם חֶלְקָם בַּחַיִּים [תְּהִלִּים יז, יד]
He said to them, "Their portion is in life" (Tehillim 17:14).
for you are destined for the life of the World to Come."
וְכִי זֶה תַּכְלִית שְׂכָרוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
is this, then, the ultimate reward of Rabbi Akiva,
that he is destined for the life of the World to Come —
מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ גַּם עַל הַהוּא כּוֹבֵס
something they said even about that launderer
וְעַל קְטִיעָה בַּר שָׁלוֹם (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה י, ב)
and about Ketia bar Shalom (Avodah Zarah 10b)?
It is like what they asked in the Gemara (Pesachim 50a)
on what they said, "The martyrs of the kingdom —
no person can stand in their compartment":
"If you say Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues,
מִשּׁוּם הֲרוּגֵי מַלְכוּת וְתוּ לָא וְכוּלֵּי
is it because they were martyrs of the kingdom and nothing more?" etc.
וְאָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן קִסְמָא
and Rabbi Yosei ben Kisma said to him,
תָּמֵהַּ אֲנִי אִם לֹא יִשְׂרְפוּ וְכוּלֵּי
"I wonder if they will not burn," etc.;
what am I regarding the life of the World to Come?"
אָמַר לוֹ כְּלוּם מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לְיָדְךָ וְכוּלֵּי
He said to him, "Has any deed come to your hand?" etc.
The wonder is that he was in doubt
whether he was destined for the life of the World to Come.
that according to the halachah it is possible
that they were not required to give up their lives,
for even regarding the three cardinal sins,
"Thus I have received from Yeshayah my teacher:
חֲבִי כִמְעַט רֶגַע וְגוֹמֵר [יְשַׁעְיָה כו, כ]
wished to sanctify the Name of Heaven;
One may say that it is like the case of
אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּכִבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ
Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, in the fiery furnace:
שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה מְצוּוֶּה עַל קְדוּשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם
he was not commanded concerning sanctification of the Name,
only he wished to sanctify the Name of Heaven
for the need of the hour,
אַף שֶׁמִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחוּיָּב בַּדָּבָר וְנֶהֱרַג
even though one who is not obligated in the matter and is killed
is liable for his life according to the Rambam
(הִלְכוֹת יְסוֹדֵי הַתּוֹרָה פֶּרֶק ה הֲלָכָה ד)
בְּעִנְיַן רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן תְּרַדְיוֹן
regarding Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon,
that possibly they were not permitted to,
by the law against taking one's own life,
and they should have hidden themselves,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁאַל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן קִסְמָא
just as Rabbi Yosei ben Kisma asked
לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן תְּרַדְיוֹן [עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שָׁם]
of Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon (Avodah Zarah, ibid.),
and Pappus of Rabbi Akiva (Berachos, ibid.).
"If in the place of our life
because he sensed in his soul
that it was necessary for it to come to his hand
and this is the essence of his life
and the elevation of his soul, as mentioned above.
This is akin to a transgression for the sake of Heaven,
that it is like a mitzvah not for its own sake;
"Length of days is in its right hand,
in its left, riches and honor":
for those who go to the right,
who engage in Torah and mitzvos for their own sake —
length of days, in the World to Come,
and for those who go to the left,
who engage not for its own sake —
riches and honor in this world there are,
but not length of days in the World to Come
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שַׁבָּת סג, א וְעַיֵּין רַשִׁ״י שָׁם)
(as stated in Shabbos 63a; see Rashi there).
which was akin to a transgression for the sake of Heaven,
אִם עַל זֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ יַגִּיעַ שָׂכָר לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
whether for this itself a reward would come in the World to Come.
וְעַל זֶה הֵשִׁיב הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
And to this HaKadosh Baruch Hu answered,
that from the portion of this very deed
to ascend to the level of "in thought before Me."
And regarding this the heavenly voice went forth:
for you are destined for the life of the World to Come" —
for this is his ultimate bliss

paragraphs.text: Tanchuma, Ki Seitzei 11 — “Rabbi Berechyah said in Rabbi Abba bar Kahana’s name: As long as Amalek’s offspring exist, it is as though a covering-wing conceals the face. When his offspring are gone from the world, ‘Your Teacher will no longer be concealed.’” The first image concerns the hidden Teacher; the second concerns the incomplete Name and throne. Rav Tzadok explains the former through the light of the Oral Torah.

paragraphs.text: Menachot 29b — “Moshe returned before the Holy One, blessed be He, and said: Master of the world, You have such a person, and You give the Torah through me? He said: Be silent; so it arose in thought before Me. Moshe said: You have shown me his Torah; show me his reward. He said: Turn around. Moshe turned and saw Rabbi Akiva’s flesh being weighed in the market. He said: Master of the world, this is Torah and this its reward? He said: Be silent; so it arose in thought before Me.” The passage follows Moshe’s vision of Rabbi Akiva expounding the crowns of letters. Rav Tzadok’s reading of “before Me” as a level beyond thought is the maamar’s mystical interpretation of the divine response.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Shaar HaGilgulim, Introduction 35, paragraph 9 — “The severities of Atik Yomin, which are within Arich Anpin and from which the supernal Mother emerged, become revealed long before the kindnesses. One who is of this second aspect of the root of Kayin can ascend from degree to degree, from severity to severity, until the severity of Atik Yomin, and draw from there. This is why the Midrash says, ‘Every precious thing his eye saw’—Rabbi Akiva: things not revealed to Moshe were revealed to Rabbi Akiva. The root of Hevel can attain the crowns of the letters, the tags, while this aspect of Kayin can attain the cantillation, or higher still. Nevertheless, Moshe our teacher subsequently attained everything through his immense deeds.” The Ari’s transmitted teaching links the very Midrash cited here to Rabbi Akiva’s capacity to ascend to Atik Yomin. It gives a precise background for Rav Tzadok’s explanation of Akiva’s soul-root and attainment, while retaining the source’s qualification that Moshe ultimately attained all through his deeds. Rav Tzadok states outright in Pri Tzaddik, Lag BaOmer 1, that Rabbi Akiva was the root of Torah she'b'al peh, “as is stated in the writings of the Arizal.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Beshalach 11 — “‘In thought before Me’ — that is Atika, which is before thought… and why He said to him ‘Be silent’: through silence one merits the secret of Da’as… the inner depth of Keser.” Rav Tzadok there reads the same Gemara of Moshe and Rabbi Akiva. He adds that the very command “Be silent” is the way to this level, since Atika is reached only by “belimah,” restraining mouth and heart.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 61b — “When they took Rabbi Akiva out to be killed, it was the time for the Shema. They combed his flesh with iron combs, and he accepted the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven. His students asked: Our master, even to this point? He answered: All my days I was troubled over ‘with all your soul’—even if He takes your soul. I said: When will it come to my hand and I fulfill it? Now that it has come to my hand, shall I not fulfill it? He prolonged ‘One’ until his soul departed with ‘One.’ A heavenly voice proclaimed: Fortunate are you, Rabbi Akiva, that your soul departed with One.” The disciples’ question and Rabbi Akiva’s answer are essential to Rav Tzadok’s interpretation: his final declaration completes a lifelong aspiration to cleave to Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Sotah 36b — “At that moment the image of his father appeared to him in the window. He said: Yosef, your brothers are destined to be inscribed upon the stones of the ephod, and you among them. Do you wish your name to be erased from among them? Immediately his bow returned to its strength. ‘His arms became agile’: He planted his hands in the ground, and his seed issued from between his fingernails. It was taught: Twelve tribes should have issued from Yosef as from his father Yaakov, but because of this emission they did not; nevertheless they issued from his brother Binyamin, and all were named in relation to Yosef.” The Bavli describes the fingernails and the loss of ten potential tribes. The ten sparks and their relation to the martyrs are explained in Tikkunei Zohar, quoted next.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 69, 110a–b — “In this yud Yosef sinned: ‘His bow remained firm, and his arms became agile.’ What is ‘became agile’? A drop, which is yud, was cast between the ten fingers and divided into ten sparks cast from the bow, which is the covenant. Where were they cast? Into the ten martyrs. He asked: Have we not heard that the ten martyrs were Yaakov’s sons? He answered: Heaven forbid; rather, they were in their image. Yosef received his consequence through these ten martyrs, corresponding to the ten tribes that should have issued from him.” This account distinguishes the martyrs from a literal identification as Yaakov’s sons and explains the number through Yosef’s unrealized ten tribes. It is the specific kabbalistic interpretation used in this maamar.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Arizal, Shaar Maamarei Razal, Shabbos — “‘Every precious thing his eye saw’ — this is Rabbi Akiva… for he and his colleagues, of the Ten Martyrs, came from the drops that Yosef cast… and ‘yakar’ is the letters of ‘keri.’” The Arizal makes explicit the root Rav Tzadok assumes here. The souls of the Ten Martyrs are those very drops of Yosef, so their death rectified the one flaw that left an opening for Amalek’s charge against the covenant.

paragraphs.text: Kesubos 103b — “On the day of Rabbi’s funeral a heavenly voice proclaimed: Everyone present at Rabbi’s funeral is prepared for the life of the world to come. A certain launderer used to come before him every day, but that day he did not come. When he heard this he went up to the roof, fell to the ground, and died. A heavenly voice proclaimed: That launderer too is prepared for the life of the world to come.” Rav Tzadok cites the repeated formula “prepared for the life of the world to come” in order to ask what specific addition that formula conveys in Rabbi Akiva’s case.

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 10b — “A heavenly voice went out and said: Ketiya bar Shalom is prepared for the life of the world to come. Rabbi wept and said: One acquires his world in a single hour, and another acquires his world over many years.” The narrative concerns Ketiya’s defense of Israel before the emperor and his subsequent death. Its use of the same formula sharpens the question about Rabbi Akiva’s announcement.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 50a — “I heard that those killed by the kingdom are of such a level that no person can stand in their enclosure. Who are they? If you say Rabbi Akiva and his companions—is it only because they were killed by the kingdom, and nothing more? Rather, it refers to those killed at Lod.” The Gemara itself rejects making Rabbi Akiva’s stature depend solely on the manner of his death. That is the force of Rav Tzadok’s comparison.

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 18a — “Rabbi Yosei ben Kisma said: I speak to you with reason, and you answer me, ‘Heaven will have mercy’? I would be surprised if they do not burn you and the Torah scroll in fire. Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon asked: My master, what is my portion in the world to come? He asked: Has any deed come to your hand? He answered: Money for Purim became mixed with charity money, and I distributed it to the poor. He said: If so, may my portion be from your portion and my lot from your lot.” The exchange concerns Rabbi Chanina’s continued public teaching under persecution. Rav Tzadok considers why a further deed is asked about despite his manifest devotion to Torah.

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:8 — “Chananyah, Mishael and Azaryah went to Yechezkel and asked whether they should bow to the image. He answered: I have received from Yeshayahu my teacher, ‘Hide for a little moment until the wrath passes.’ They said: Do you wish that people should say every nation bowed to this image? He asked what they proposed. They answered: We wish to expose its defect by being there and refusing to bow, so that people will say all the nations bow to this image except Israel. He said: If that is your intention, wait until I consult the divine Power.” The Midrash distinguishes hiding from deliberately appearing at the idolatrous ceremony. Rav Tzadok invokes that distinction in his speculative explanation of the exceptional public sanctification undertaken by the sages.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Cf. R. Avraham de Boton, Lechem Mishneh, Hilchos Yesodei HaTorah 5:4 — “The Ran found no resolution for Elisha’s self-sacrifice except that it was an act of piety. But our master holds that one who is not required to die and nevertheless does so incurs liability for his own life. How, then, did Elisha act? One may answer that our master holds that Elisha was required to surrender his life. … Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon surrendered his life to engage in Torah. … Although the Ran can resolve all these cases as he resolved Elisha’s, our master does not accept that approach: for him there is no special measure of piety here; all these figures surrendered their lives because they were obligated.”

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 61b — “Pappus found Rabbi Akiva gathering assemblies publicly and teaching Torah. He asked: Are you not afraid of the kingdom? Akiva answered with a parable: A fox saw fish fleeing from the nets people cast upon them. He invited them to leave the river and live with him on dry land. They answered: You are called clever, yet you are foolish! If we fear in the place of our life, how much more in the place of our death. So too, if we fear while studying Torah, of which it says, ‘It is your life and the length of your days,’ how much more if we abandon it.” The parable explains why withdrawing from Torah is not a safer form of life. Rav Tzadok reads Akiva’s answer together with his lifelong wish to fulfill “with all your soul.”

paragraphs.text: Nazir 23b — “Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: A transgression for the sake of Heaven is greater than a mitzvah performed not for its own sake. But Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: A person should always engage in Torah and mitzvos even not for their own sake, because from not for their own sake he comes to act for their own sake. Rather, say: It is like a mitzvah performed not for its own sake. For it is written, ‘Blessed among women is Yael, wife of Chever the Kenite; among women in the tent she shall be blessed.’” The Gemara corrects “greater than” to “like.” Rav Tzadok preserves that correction in comparing the special act here with a mitzvah not performed for its own sake.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 63a; Rashi, s.v. Lamayminin and Lamasme’ilin — “‘Length of days is in her right hand; in her left, wealth and honor.’ Does the right have length of days but not wealth and honor? Rather: For those who take the right side in Torah, there is length of days, and certainly wealth and honor. For those who take the left side, there is wealth and honor, but no length of days.” Rashi first explains the right side as scrutinizing Torah’s reasons carefully and selecting them skillfully, while the left neglects sufficient effort. He then gives an alternative: the right studies for its own sake, the left not for its own sake. Rav Tzadok uses this second explanation.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 61b — “The ministering angels said before the Holy One, blessed be He: This is Torah, and this its reward? ‘From men, by Your hand, Hashem; from men ...’! He answered: ‘Their portion is in life.’ A heavenly voice proclaimed: Fortunate are you, Rabbi Akiva, that you are prepared for the life of the world to come.” The maamar returns to these concluding words after asking what the promise adds to Akiva’s already assured stature. It reads “their portion” as the spiritual attainment effected through this very act.
